created: 2026-10-21 (task-64): the capability bank. Every question is of the shape 'can X do Y', and every one is built from the corpus rather than from imagination - the answer record and the decoy were found by searching for sentences that grant the capability (see workspace/t64-scan.mjs). The 33-question bank measures retrieval; this one measures APPLICABILITY: whether the record the judge rests on actually reaches the subject of the question.
note: Fields: q, kind, answer (the record that ACTUALLY applies, or null when the honest answer is no and no single record is the answer), decoy (a record that grants the same capability to something else - the record a judge cites when it does not check the scope), yes (the honest answer), reason (why, so a later reader can check the bank rather than trust it), scope (the phrase in the record that decides applicability). scopeSource names the record the scope phrase is quoted from when the question's honest answer is no and the rule that decides it is a general one rather than a record about the subject. THE CONDITIONAL-YES SEMANTICS (task-82), which cases 5 and 6 exist to test: a grant has a SUBJECT and often a CONDITION, and the two are read separately. A grant that reaches the SUBJECT of the question under a condition is a YES, and the answer must state the condition in the same sentence because the condition is the answer - never a bare "Yes". A grant that reaches a DIFFERENT subject is a NO, however similar the wording. Cases 5 and 6 rest on the same record, the Rampart Crest (unitrules#000002594~3), and have opposite answers: it gives a 5+ invulnerable save to "models in that unit" while the bearer is leading a unit, so a unit led by a Kahl has it (6, yes, and the condition is the answer) and so does the Kahl in the attached unit it leads, because core-rules#Abilities-in-Attached-Units makes an attached unit a single unit for all rules purposes and a leader keeps benefiting from its own ‘while this model is leading a unit’ abilities (5, conditional yes; ALSO CONFOUNDED, since the Kahl datasheet carries inv 4+, which is why the pair is kept only as a known-confounded record and the different-subject half is carried by the scope decoys). A verdict that is right on one half and wrong on the other is the failure this pair exists to catch. RE-SCORED AND EXTENDED (task-82, second pass): the bank had scored EVERY conditional grant as no, which is the error the app must not make - a grant that reaches the subject under a condition is a yes (cases 5, 8, 9 re-scored), a grant that reaches a different subject is a no. Case 5 is kept as a KNOWN-CONFOUNDED record (the Kahl datasheet already carries inv 4+); case 10 was reworded to what the rule decides; case 16 is the default rule, with faction-rule#000009994 named as the exception it does not cover. Three scope cases were added (Onager aura vs Baneblade, Sanctifiers vs attached priest, Deathstrike after Advancing) so the bank still measures applicability rather than agreement. THIRD PASS (task-82): the Deathstrike case was a SECOND bank error of the same shape - ‘can a Deathstrike shoot after it moved?’ is a yes for the unit (normal shooting needs only that it did not Advance, and the missile’s Remained Stationary restriction reaches the missile, not the unit), so the question now names the missile; the ‘turn in which it Advanced’ case keeps its no but its reason moved to NORMAL/ASSAULT SHOOTING; and three more scope decoys joined (Enginseer vs an Infantry squad, Abaddon’s aura vs DAMNED, Firing Deck vs a Land Raider).

questions.q: Can a baneblade have an invulnerable save?
questions.scope: one friendly Astra Militarum Vehicle model within 3" of this model
questions.reason: The Astra Militarum Tech-Priest Enginseer's Omnissiah's Blessing gives 'that VEHICLE model' a 4+ invulnerable save, and a Baneblade is an Astra Militarum Vehicle. The Baneblade's own datasheet lists no InSv, which is what makes the negative look safe. DECOYS: the Tech-priest Manipulus's Defend the Divine Work gives a 4+ invulnerable save to 'all models in this model's unit' and a Manipulus cannot join a Baneblade; the Onager Dunecrawler's Emanatus Force Field gives one to an ADEPTUS MECHANICUS BATTLELINE model, which a Baneblade is not. This is Mandal's own case and the model for the bank.

questions.q: Can a baneblade use the Onager Dunecrawler's Emanatus Force Field?
questions.scope: a friendly ADEPTUS MECHANICUS BATTLELINE model wholly within 6"
questions.reason: The aura reaches ADEPTUS MECHANICUS BATTLELINE models only. A Baneblade is ASTRA MILITARUM and not BATTLELINE, so the aura cannot apply however close it stands. An honest no that a decoy-shaped record could turn into a yes.

questions.q: Does a Tech-priest Manipulus give its own unit an invulnerable save?
questions.scope: all models in this model’s unit
questions.reason: Defend the Divine Work: 'until the end of the phase, all models in this model's unit have a 4+ invulnerable save'. The scope is the Manipulus's own unit, so it applies. A judge that treats every '4+ invulnerable save' sentence as interchangeable answers this one right by accident - it is in the bank to separate that from the Baneblade case.

questions.q: Can an Einhyr Champion have a 4+ invulnerable save?
questions.scope: the bearer
questions.reason: Weavefield Crest: 'The bearer has a 4+ invulnerable save'. The scope is the bearer, and the Einhyr Champion is the bearer. DECOY: the Hearthkyn Warriors' Weavefield Crest gives 'models in the bearer's unit' a 5+ invulnerable save - a different scope and a different value, and a judge that reads 'Weavefield Crest' as one thing will cite the wrong one.

questions.q: Can a Kahl have an invulnerable save from its Rampart Crest?
questions.scope: while the bearer is leading a unit, models in that unit
questions.reason: RE-SCORED task-82. The Rampart Crest is "While the bearer is leading a unit, models in that unit have a 5+ invulnerable save" - a unit-affecting ability, so it reaches the Kahl in the attached unit it leads. CORPUS: core-rules#Abilities-in-Attached-Units - "abilities/rules that affect a unit (or models in it) apply to every model in an attached unit", and a leader "continues to benefit from its own while this model is leading a unit abilities". A grant that reaches the SUBJECT under a condition is a YES; a grant that reaches a DIFFERENT subject is a NO. The old reason ("the Kahl is the leader, not a model in the unit it leads") is FALSE and is removed: an attached unit is a single unit for all rules purposes. THIS CASE IS ALSO CONFOUNDED - the Kahl datasheet carries inv 4+, so the question cannot distinguish whether the crest reaches it - and it is kept only as a known-confounded record, with the unconfounded scope cases below doing the measuring.

questions.q: Does a unit led by a Kahl have a 5+ invulnerable save?
questions.scope: While the bearer is leading a unit
questions.reason: The other half of the Rampart Crest pair. Yes, and the answer record is the same one the previous question must NOT use.

questions.q: Can a Hearthkyn Warriors unit have a 5+ invulnerable save?
questions.scope: Models in the bearer’s unit
questions.reason: The Hearthkyn Warriors' Weavefield Crest gives 'models in the bearer's unit' a 5+ invulnerable save. DECOY: the Einhyr Champion's Weavefield Crest gives the bearer alone a 4+ - same name, narrower scope, different value.

questions.q: Does an Autarch have the Scouts ability?
questions.scope: while this model is leading a Striking Scorpions unit
questions.reason: RE-SCORED task-82. unitrules#000000577~2: "While this model is leading a Striking Scorpions unit, it has the Infiltrators, Scouts 7" and Stealth abilities." The subject is THIS MODEL and the condition is leading that unit, so the grant reaches the subject. CORPUS: core-rules#Abilities-in-Attached-Units - "abilities/rules that affect a unit (or models in it) apply to every model in an attached unit", and a leader "continues to benefit from its own while this model is leading a unit abilities". A grant that reaches the SUBJECT under a condition is a YES; a grant that reaches a DIFFERENT subject is a NO. The old reason ("a conditional grant is not a keyword the Autarch always has") is the wrong test and is removed.

questions.q: Does a Ministorum Priest have the Scouts ability?
questions.scope: if this model is attached to a DOMINION SQUAD
questions.reason: RE-SCORED task-82. unitrules#000001553~2: "If this model is attached to a DOMINION SQUAD during the Declare Battle Formations step, it gains the Scouts 6" ability." The subject is THIS MODEL under a condition, so it is a conditional yes. CORPUS: core-rules#Abilities-in-Attached-Units - "abilities/rules that affect a unit (or models in it) apply to every model in an attached unit", and a leader "continues to benefit from its own while this model is leading a unit abilities". A grant that reaches the SUBJECT under a condition is a YES; a grant that reaches a DIFFERENT subject is a NO.

questions.q: Can a Sanctifiers unit make a scout move?
questions.scope: Ability (Core): Scouts
questions.reason: REWORDED task-82. The old question ("set up in ambush") turned on a phrase the rule does not settle, and its reason ("the unit itself does not have Scouts") was FALSE: the Sanctifiers own keywords-and-abilities record lists "Ability (Core): Scouts" (unitrules#000004075~1, and 000004074~1 in Imperial Agents). The unit has Scouts natively, so a scout move is a plain YES, and the attached-priest grant (000004075~3, "that model gains the Scouts 6" ability") is the DECOY - the grant runs the other way, to the attached model.

questions.q: Can a Starweaver's passengers shoot?
questions.scope: units embarked within this TRANSPORT
questions.reason: Firing Deck lets embarked passengers shoot through the transport. The answer record is the Starweaver's own keyword list, which carries the Firing Deck entry - the third task-57 question in the 33-bank expects this record, so the bank shares one case with the retrieval set on purpose.

questions.q: Can a Wraithguard unit shoot after it Fell Back?
questions.scope: This unit is eligible to shoot in a turn in which it Fell Back
questions.reason: War Construct states it outright for this unit. DECOY: the Ironstrider Ballistarii's Elevated Strider says the same for a different unit - both are real grants, and the question is which one the question's subject is. The core rule (FALL-BACK MOVE) says a unit that Fell Back is not eligible to shoot, which is the honest no for every unit without such a rule.

questions.q: Can an Astra Militarum infantry squad shoot after it Fell Back?
questions.scope: not eligible to shoot
questions.reason: FALL-BACK MOVE makes a unit that Fell Back ineligible to shoot, and no Astra Militarum infantry datasheet in the corpus carries a grant. The decoys are two real grants that belong to other units - the exact citation a judge reaches for when it does not check the subject.

questions.q: Can a Deathstrike fire its Deathstrike missile after it moved?
questions.scope: only if it Remained Stationary this turn
questions.reason: REWORDED task-82, third pass: the old question was a BANK ERROR, and the agent's yes was right. A unit that made a normal move is still eligible to shoot - NORMAL SHOOTING at core-rules#Shooting-Phase->-3.-End-of-Shooting-Phase->-NORMAL-SHOOTING is 'eligible if your unit is unengaged and did not make an advance move this turn' - and the Deathstrike carries a heavy bolter, a heavy flamer and a hunter-killer missile, so the honest answer for the unit is YES. The Restriction in unitrules#000000699 reaches the weapon, not the unit: 'Plasma Warhead - The bearer can only shoot with this weapon in your Shooting phase, and only if it Remained Stationary this turn.' The question now names the missile, so the no is honest and its scope decides it. This is the same instrument error as case 10: the question did not name the subject the rule is about.

questions.q: Does a unit have to Remain Stationary to fire a Hazardous weapon?
questions.scope: Remained Stationary
questions.reason: Hazardous weapons have no such restriction. The corpus holds no [HAZARDOUS] keyword definition record - only the hazard-roll procedure and FAQ entries - and the 'Remained Stationary' restriction in the corpus belongs to the Deathstrike's own missile, not to Hazardous weapons. A judge that finds both words on one record answers yes; the decoy is that record. NOTE FOR A LATER READER: the absence of a [HAZARDOUS] definition record is itself a corpus gap, not a bank error.

questions.q: Can a unit that Fell Back declare a charge?
questions.scope: not eligible to shoot, declare a charge or start an action
questions.reason: REWORDED task-82. The old reason rested on the core rule alone and the corpus holds faction overrides: faction-rule#000009994 grants an Emperor’s Children unit "eligible to shoot and declare a charge in a turn in which it Advanced or Fell Back". So the honest answer to the GENERIC question is no and the honest answer to "can it, with a named exception" is a conditional yes, and the bank cannot have it both ways. The question is now the DEFAULT rule, which the corpus states outright.

questions.q: Can an Onager Dunecrawler give a Baneblade an invulnerable save?
questions.scope: While a friendly ADEPTUS MECHANICUS BATTLELINE model is wholly within 6" of this model
questions.reason: NEW task-82, the scope split. unitrules#000000854~2: "Emanatus Force Field (Aura) - While a friendly ADEPTUS MECHANICUS BATTLELINE model is wholly within 6" of this model, that BATTLELINE model has a 4+ invulnerable save." The aura reaches ADEPTUS MECHANICUS BATTLELINE models only. A Baneblade is ASTRA MILITARUM and not BATTLELINE, so the grant reaches a different subject and the answer is NO however close it stands. The decoy is that record itself, cited without the scope.

questions.q: Does a Sanctifiers unit gain the Scouts ability from an attached Ministorum Priest?
questions.scope: that model gains the Scouts 6" ability
questions.reason: NEW task-82, the scope split, and the mirror of case 8. unitrules#000004075~3: "If a MINISTORUM PRIEST from your army is attached to this unit during the Declare Battle Formations step, THAT MODEL gains the Scouts 6" ability." The grant runs the other way: the priest gains it, the unit does not, so the subject of the question is outside the grant. NO. The decoy is the record a judge cites when it reads the grant without its subject.

questions.q: Can a Deathstrike shoot in a turn in which it Advanced?
questions.scope: did not make an advance move this turn
questions.reason: REASON CORRECTED task-82, third pass. The no is right; the old reason reached it by the wrong route. A unit that Advanced may not fire normally: NORMAL SHOOTING at core-rules#Shooting-Phase->-3.-End-of-Shooting-Phase->-NORMAL-SHOOTING is eligible only for a unit that 'did not make an advance move this turn', and ASSAULT SHOOTING needs one or more [ASSAULT] weapons, which no Deathstrike weapon carries. So the Deathstrike cannot shoot at all that turn, and the missile's Remained Stationary restriction (unitrules#000000699) is a second, independent bar rather than the deciding one. The decoy is that record, cited without the shooting-type rule that actually settles it.

questions.q: Can a Cadian Shock Troops squad have an invulnerable save from a Tech-Priest Enginseer?
questions.scope: select one friendly Astra Militarum Vehicle model within 3"
questions.reason: NEW task-82, third pass, the scope split, and the mirror of case 1. unitrules#000001396: 'Omnissiah’s Blessing - In your Command phase, select one friendly Astra Militarum Vehicle model within 3" of this model. That VEHICLE model regains up to D3 lost wounds and, until the start of your next Command phase, that VEHICLE model has a 4+ invulnerable save.' The scope is VEHICLE. A Cadian Shock Troops squad (unitrules#000002612, keywords ASTRA MILITARUM, INFANTRY, BATTLELINE) carries no invulnerable save of its own, so the grant reaches a different subject: NO. The same record answers case 1 YES for a Baneblade - one record, two answers, decided by the scope.

questions.q: Does an Accursed Cultists unit within 6" of Abaddon the Despoiler have a 4+ invulnerable save?
questions.scope: excluding DAMNED units
questions.reason: NEW task-82, third pass, the scope split. unitrules#000000924~2: 'Mark of Chaos Ascendant (Aura) - While a friendly Heretic Astartes Infantry or Heretic Astartes Mounted unit (excluding DAMNED units) is within 6" of this model, models in that unit have a 4+ invulnerable save.' Accursed Cultists (unitrules#000002571~1) carry the Damned keyword, so the aura’s own exclusion puts them outside it: NO. The decoy is that record, cited without its 'excluding DAMNED units' clause - the same join failure the bank exists to catch, on a keyword the scope EXCLUDES rather than one it names.

questions.q: Can a unit embarked within a Land Raider shoot?
questions.scope: if one or more units are embarked within it
questions.reason: NEW task-82, third pass, the scope split. Firing Deck travels with the transport’s own record, not with the TRANSPORT keyword: unitrules#000002541~1 (Starweaver) carries 'Ability (Core): Firing Deck', while the Space Marines Land Raider (unitrules#000000065~1 and ~2) carries none. A unit embarked in a transport is not on the battlefield, and core-rules#2.-Shoot makes eligibility to shoot require being on the battlefield, so a Land Raider’s passengers cannot shoot: NO. The decoy is the Starweaver record - a real grant of the same capability to the passengers of a different transport, which is what a judge cites when it reads the ability and not the transport it belongs to.
